name: CA-44
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 20 points on the partisan voting index
Incumbent Nanette Barragán has a massive financial edge, with over $1 million on hand versus under $10,000 for her Republican opponent
Prediction markets price Barragán's win probability at roughly 97 percent
No competitive polling or expert ratings exist, but no evidence suggests a race
model.rationale: This is a heavily Democratic district where Barragán enjoys incumbency, a roughly 56-to-1 fundraising advantage, and outside support while her opponent has raised under $14,000. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy incumbent win, so the forecast stays at a wide Democratic margin.
model.watch: The only meaningful risk is a surprise red-wave environment or an unforeseen scandal, but with no polling or spending against her, Barragán's position is unlikely to change.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nanette Barragán, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Southern California district that leans about 20 points Democratic. She advanced to the general election and faces Republican Genevieve Angel, a first-time challenger with minimal resources. Barragán has raised roughly $786,000 and holds more than $1 million in cash, while Angel has raised under $14,000 and has no outside support.

No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets give Barragán about a 97 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's partisan lean, her incumbency, and her overwhelming financial advantage makes this one of the safest Democratic seats on the ballot, with only a remote chance of an upset.
